meaning:
ἐκκακέω, -ῶ, see: ἐνκακέω.
ἐν-κακέω, -ῶ (LTr., ἐγκ-; Rec. ἐκκ-; cf. WH, Notes, 157 f.; κακός, cowardly),
[in Sm.: Gen.27:46, Num.21:5, Pro.3:11, Isa.7:16 *;]
to lose heart : Luk.18:1, 2Co.4:1,16, Gal.6:9, Eph.3:13, 2Th.3:13 (Cremer, 330).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,
Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.
Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
Therefore I ask that you may not lose heart at my troubles for you, which are your glory.
But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
